leaf_morphology.secondary_veins: highly visible, prominent, and regularly spaced

traits.notes: The leaves have a distinctively rugose (quilted) texture due to the prominent, sunken secondary veins. The overall growth habit appears to be a small, clustered seedling.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides, as seen in images 2 and 5)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely packed at the apex of the stem, forming a rosette-like appearance)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided and attached directly to the stem via a petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaf edges are smooth and continuous without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are widest below the middle and taper towards the tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the tip tapers gradually to a slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaf tapers gradually to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): highly visible, prominent, and regularly spaced (the lateral veins are distinct and run parallel to each other towards the margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, rugose (the surface is glossy and textured with sunken veins giving a quilted appearance)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (the surface appears smooth and glabrous under magnification)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles are clearly visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears green, slender, and non-woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: green (the stem is uniformly green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no visible ridges, lenticels, or roughness)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are present)
F. Notes: The leaves have a distinctively rugose (quilted) texture due to the prominent, sunken secondary veins. The overall growth habit appears to be a small, clustered seedling.
